description_good_justification: The README and the website open with what the project does: run compute tasks wherever they run best, locally, in a Web Worker or on a remote service, with one API: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/
interact_justification: The website and README explain how to get the packages (npm), give feedback (GitHub issues) and contribute: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: The contribution process (issues, pull requests, checks, sign-off): https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
contribution_requirements_justification: Contribution requirements, including coding style and tests, are in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
documentation_basics_justification: Guides for getting started and for each backend: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/guide/introduction/
documentation_interface_justification: The API reference, generated from the source with TypeDoc: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/api/
sites_https_justification: The repository, the npm packages and the documentation site are served over HTTPS: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports and comments in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with releases and changes in October 2026: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change is a public commit and pull request between releases, not only the releases themselves.
version_unique_justification: Every release of each package has a unique version, tagged as @hybrid-compute/<package>@<version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, each package versioned on its own; below 1.0 a breaking change bumps the minor version.
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/tags
release_notes_justification: Each package has a CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability in the published packages. Such a fix would be listed in the release notes and a GitHub security advisory.
report_responses_justification: Every issue is assigned to the maintainer and triaged when it is opened; there have been no unanswered bug reports in the last 12 months.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their GitHub issue; there have been none from outside the project in the last 12 months without a response.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests stay public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Reports are acknowledged within 7 days; no vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
build_justification: npm run build compiles every package with tsc -b: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/guide/development
build_floss_tools_justification: npm, Node.js and TypeScript are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Each package has a node:test suite, run with npm test; the release scripts have their own (npm run test:scripts).
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard way to run tests in an npm project.
test_most_justification: Line coverage: core 87%, local 100%, remote 89%, worker 84%; coverage is uploaded to Codecov from every CI run.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Checks workflow builds and tests every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
test_policy_justification: New functionality must come with tests and bug fixes with a regression test: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with tests, e.g. the release plan tests added with the release script in #116.
tests_documented_added_justification: The tests policy is part of the instructions for contributing code: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: TypeScript runs in strict mode, ESLint (typescript-eslint and stylistic rules) on all code, and TypeDoc treats warnings as errors.
warnings_fixed_justification: Lint has no errors; the two remaining warnings are one console call in core, scheduled for the core API review (#82).
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript runs with strict: true, TypeDoc treats warnings as errors in CI, and lint errors fail the Checks workflow. The only lint warnings are the core console call tracked in #82.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows how to design secure software; the principles applied are in the assurance case: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles
know_common_errors_justification: The common weaknesses for this kind of software and how they are countered: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#common-weaknesses-countered
crypto_published_justification: The packages implement no cryptography. The remote backend uses the runtime's fetch and WebSocket, so TLS, its versions and certificate verification are handled by the browser or Node.js; the project never disables verification, and the security policy says to use https: and wss: endpoints: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

delivery_mitm_justification: Packages are delivered by npm over HTTPS with Sigstore-signed provenance, and the repository by GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; npm verifies package integrity from the registry metadata over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The published packages have no known vulnerabilities (npm audit --omit=dev runs before every release). Development tooling alerts are fixed or accepted as described in the security policy: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been found in the published packages.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses every pull request and push to main, and ESLint runs on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL analyses the JavaScript/TypeScript code and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; the ruleset blocks merging with a high or critical one.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or property-based testing yet; property-based tests are planned for 1.0 (#88).
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: All software is TypeScript on JavaScript runtimes, which are memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The packages do not use run-time assertions beyond their error checks; input validation is decided in the 1.0 API reviews (#82 to #85).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run yet, so it has found nothing to fix.
achieve_passing_justification: The project has the passing badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15720
dco_justification: Every commit must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked on every pull request by the DCO app: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: The maintainer-led governance model and how decisions are made: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities, and who holds them: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer holds the access to the repository, npm organisation and domain today. Releases use npm trusted publishing (no personal token) and the code is MIT-licensed, but no second person holds access yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: What the project plans to do, and not do, until October 2027, with the work tracked in GitHub issues and the 1.0 milestone: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: Packages, dispatch, message formats, design, build and release: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/guide/architecture
documentation_security_justification: What users can and cannot rely on: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
documentation_current_justification: The API reference is generated from the source with TypeDoc at every release, and CI fails on TypeDoc warnings such as broken links (npm run docs:check). Documentation defects are fixed as normal changes.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README links the OpenSSF Scorecard and Best Practices badges: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The docs site uses VitePress semantic HTML, light and dark themes whose text and colour pairs all pass WCAG AA contrast, and real buttons with accessible names for its interactive parts. The packages have no user interface.
internationalization_justification: The packages return task results, not text for end users, and do not sort human-readable text.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub, npm and a static docs site) store no passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Below 1.0 the latest release of each package is supported; from 1.0 each major is supported as a whole, the previous major gets high and critical security fixes for 6 months, and deprecated APIs keep working for one full major: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been reported to the project in the last 12 months; the repository has no security advisories.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Reports are made privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email. Acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment, a fix in a private GitHub security advisory, coordinated disclosure and credit: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: Code follows the project ESLint configuration (eslint-config-phun-ky), Prettier and strict TypeScript, and must pass npm run lint, npm run format:check and npm run typecheck: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The Checks workflow runs ESLint, Prettier and the TypeScript compiler in strict mode on every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires it to pass before merging.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are built; the project compiles TypeScript to JavaScript.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The TypeScript build emits source maps and declaration maps alongside the JavaScript; nothing is stripped or minified.
build_non_recursive_justification: npm run build runs tsc -b with TypeScript project references, building each package once in dependency order.
build_repeatable_justification: The TypeScript compiler is deterministic and dependencies are pinned in package-lock.json (npm ci in CI); rebuilding the same source gives identical output.
installation_common_justification: Packages are installed and removed with npm, e.g. npm install @hybrid-compute/core and npm uninstall @hybrid-compute/core.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done entirely by npm, which honours its standard location settings (--prefix, npm_config_prefix, global vs. local). The packages have no install scripts.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm install, npm run build and npm test give the full development and test environment: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/guide/development
external_dependencies_justification: Dependencies are listed in each package.json and locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks npm dependencies and GitHub Actions weekly, dependency review checks every pull request, and npm audit runs before every release: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository; all external components come from npm through package.json and the lockfile, and Dependabot opens update pull requests.
interfaces_current_justification: The code uses current interfaces: ES modules, Node 24, TypeScript 6, fetch and WebSocket, and current GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs; deprecated compiler options were removed (baseUrl, node10 resolution).
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Checks workflow builds, lints, type-checks, checks the API docs and runs the tests on every push to main and every pull request, reporting results as GitHub checks with coverage uploaded to Codecov.
regression_tests_added50_justification: The fixes in the last six months were to packaging and release metadata (LICENSE files, the homepage URL, sibling ranges) rather than code bugs with a test; regression tests are now required for every bug fix: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Line coverage, measured with Node built-in coverage on every CI run and uploaded to Codecov: core 87%, local 100%, remote 89%, worker 84%. A CI threshold and property-based tests are planned for 1.0 (#88).
test_policy_mandated_justification: New functionality must come with tests and bug fixes with a regression test: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles applied (economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, least privilege, open design, no dynamic code): https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles

signed_releases_justification: Packages are published from GitHub Actions with npm trusted publishing and carry Sigstore-signed provenance; the signing identity comes from GitHub OIDC, not a key on npm. version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not signed; releases are verified through npm provenance instead.
input_validation_justification: core validates its backends, task names and strategies (#82), and local validates the tasks registered with it (#83); bad input is rejected with TypeError, RangeError or NoBackendError. remote and worker do not validate their own options yet, and results from workers and remote endpoints are not validated; their checks are decided in the remaining 1.0 API reviews (#84, #85), as the assurance case says: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#known-gaps
hardening_justification: Strict TypeScript, no eval or dynamic code, tasks stored in a Map (no prototype pollution), no runtime dependencies outside the monorepo, validated and frozen configuration in core, read-only CI permissions with SHA-pinned actions, and CodeQL on every change.
assurance_case_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, the common weaknesses countered and the known gaps: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The maintainer, the only person with access, uses two-factor authentication on GitHub, which GitHub requires for code contributors. Anyone given access later must use it too: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires a role to be chosen for every collaborator invited to the repository, and the governance requires the lowest role that fits: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires changes to arrive through a pull request with passing checks. Only the maintainer, as administrator, and the release workflow can bypass it.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: A separate ruleset on main, with no bypass, blocks deleting the branch and force pushes.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow interpolates untrusted metadata, such as pull request titles or branch names, into a script; github.actor is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests run on the pull_request event, where forks get no secrets. osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories when fixed: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/security/advisories
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Each job declares only the permissions it needs, e.g. the labeler has pull-requests: write and publishing has id-token: write: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/.github/workflows/label.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Workflows take no manual inputs, and the only collaborator-controlled value used, github.actor, is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: Each release is a versioned npm package and a GitHub release with the same tag, and its SBOM is named <package>-<version>.cdx.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/releases
osps_br_07_02_justification: How secrets are stored, accessed and rotated: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_03_01_justification: How to verify release integrity with npm audit signatures: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_03_02_justification: How to check that a release was built by the publish workflow in phun-ky/hybrid-compute, from its provenance: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_04_01_justification: Below 1.0, the latest release of each package is supported: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: Below 1.0, a release stops getting security updates when the next release of the same package is published: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_gv_04_01_justification: Collaborators are reviewed, including two-factor authentication, before getting escalated permissions: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every GitHub release has a CycloneDX SBOM of the package's runtime dependencies attached, generated by the publish workflow: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has a single repository, so there are no subprojects in other repositories.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: When and how the tests run, locally and in CI: https://phun-ky.net/hybrid-compute/guide/development#test-the-code
osps_qa_06_03_justification: New functionality and bug fixes must come with tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The project has one maintainer, so no non-author approval is possible yet. The ruleset will require one approval once there is a second maintainer: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_sa_03_02_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries and attack surface: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#threat-model
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Vulnerabilities in dependencies that don't affect the project are recorded as OpenVEX statements: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/vex.openvex.json
osps_vm_05_01_justification: Thresholds for fixing vulnerability and licence findings in dependencies: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Releases are blocked while a runtime dependency has a known high or critical vulnerability (npm audit in the publish workflow): https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Dependency review checks every pull request against the GitHub Advisory Database and blocks high or critical findings, as the documented policy says: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The ruleset on main blocks merging while CodeQL reports an error or a high or critical security alert: https://github.com/phun-ky/hybrid-compute/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
